reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate and partly cannot run. (1) No control beyond 'default': no random-order arm, no structural-order arm, no train/test split; 'learned' is undefined (model, features, training data absent), so a >=0.2 slope drop cannot be attributed to learning versus any reordering. (2) cryptominisat5 and kissat expose no external branching-order input (only polarity/restart/heuristic flags), so 'learned order' cannot be injected without patching the solver; Gauss-Jordan XOR reasoning in CMS also interacts with ordering, which is the idea's own stated risk. (3) S_3 with 2 summands has only 2l=8..16 free bits; at n=17..23 these are millisecond instances, mostly UNSAT (2^(2l-n) <= 2^-7 solution density), propagation counts are heavy-tailed and 5 l-points x 40 instances gives a slope SE that likely exceeds the 0.05 'unchanged' band, so prediction_if_false and the 0.2 threshold are not separated by any stated CI. SAT/UNSAT mix confounds the count. (4) Runtime is fine (1600 trivial solves, far under 18 CPU-min) and tools exist (ffd_semaev_core.build_system for char-2 S_3 ANF, python ANF->CNF-XOR, cryptominisat5); ic corpus emits S_4 (m=3) not S_3, so S_3 CNF needs a small python converter. (5) Metric: solver 'propagations' is a counted operation (acceptable, not wall time) but is solver-heuristic dependent, not structural; a structural companion (msolve -v 2 F4 max degree, or Macaulay rank/d_F via hky_last_fall_degree) is order-independent so cannot test ordering, only calibrate. (6) Scaling: the exponent is in l at fixed n<=23 with l<=8, i.e. l/n<=0.35 and far from the l~n/(m+1) regime that matters; d_F is certified only >=5 and <=k+2 in this range, so a slope in l over l=4..8 is a toy artefact and says nothing about n=131 / 130-bit; also an l-slope at fixed n is not an n-exponent, and transfer 'to n=23' is just the largest toy cell, not an extrapolation. Even a positive result is classed engineering (generic oracle bound S*T^2>=r/|Aut| untouched; variable order does not change relation shape), as the idea itself states.
fix: Redesign: (a) use m=3 (S_4, 3l unknowns) via `ic corpus --degree n --dimension l --sat K --unsat K --dir $TMPDIR/...` for n in {13,17,19,23}, l in {3..7} so 3l straddles n (the interesting regime, 3l ~ n), keeping SAT and UNSAT strata separate and reporting UNSAT-only (fixed workload: full refutation). (b) Inject order solver-agnostically by cube-and-conquer: fix the first k=ceil(l/2) variables in a given order as 2^k assumption cubes (cryptominisat5 via unit clauses), sum propagations+conflicts over all cubes; count ops, not time. (c) Arms, same cube budget: default (no cubing, plain CMS), natural order, random order (>=5 permutations), reverse order, structural heuristic (highest-index basis coefficients / most-XOR-occurrences first), and learned order (small model trained on disjoint instances/seeds, frozen before test; features: var occurrence counts in XORs, degree in ANF, basis position). Learned must beat the best of the non-learned arms, not just default. (d) Pre-register: metric = log2(median propagations) per (n,l) cell, >=40 instances/cell with paired instances across arms; slope in l by OLS over >=5 l-values with bootstrap 95% CI over instances; success only if slope(best control) - slope(learned) >= 0.2 with CI excluding 0.05, replicated on a held-out seed set, and the effect is present at the largest n and not a single cell. Also report slope against n at fixed l/n ~ 0.3 so n-trend is separate from l-trend. (e) Add structural calibration: msolve -g 2 -v 2 max F4 degree and hky_last_fall_degree d_F per cell to show whether the instance hardness is saturating (then order cannot matter beyond constants). (f) Report explicitly: toy-only, no extrapolation to n=131; classification engineering unless slope reduction persists as l/n grows, and the generic bound B*D^2<<N is not addressed. Budget ~12 CPU-min.
